newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania January trade deficit at $134.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Romania January trade deficit at $134.5 mln.

text.p: Romania's trade balance had a $134.5 million deficit in January, down from $158.3 million in the same month of 1996, the National Statistics Board (CNS) said on Friday.
"Both exports and imports went down in January, with imports dropping sharper than the fall in exports," CNS president Pavel Wagner told a news conference.
January's exports stood at $575.4 million, or 6.8 percent down year-on-year, with textiles and metals holding about 60 percent of the overall figure.
Imports were $709.9 million, falling 8.5 percent from January 1996, with minerals toping the import list.
The private sector accounted for 55.4 percent of exports in January, when it took 43.8 percent of imports.
Germany was Romania's leading trading partner in January.
Romania aims to slash the deficit in the current account -- whose main component is the trade balance -- to $1.4 billion this year from an estimated $2.3 billion last year.
NOTES -- All figures in FOB prices and subject to revisions. Last December's data do not include imports with customs documents delayed.
